title: A Radio Segment Explaining Why Ordinary Mornings Matter
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Good morning, listeners. Today's five-minute reflection is about something most of us overlook entirely, the ordinary morning we just woke up into.
Narrator: We tend to reserve our sense of wonder for extraordinary events, weddings, recoveries, unexpected good news, while treating routine mornings as background noise.
Narrator: [gently] However, if you actually examine an ordinary morning closely, it turns out to contain more coordination than almost anything we call miraculous.
Narrator: Your heart restarted its rhythm the moment you woke, without a single conscious instruction from you, and it will continue doing so for the rest of today.
Narrator: [reflective] Your lungs adjusted to the air in your room, your eyes adjusted to the light, and none of it required your permission or your effort.
Narrator: In Islamic thought, this is one meaning of tauhid rububiyyah, recognizing that Allah alone sustains and governs these processes, even the ones we never consciously notice.
Narrator: [honestly] I used to think tauhid was mainly about avoiding certain sins or holding correct beliefs during difficult, dramatic moments.
Narrator: As a result, I ignored the quieter, constant evidence available every single morning, evidence that required no crisis to appear.
Narrator: [calmly] Despite how unremarkable a Tuesday morning feels, your body just completed a process more intricate than any machine humans have ever built.
Narrator: If we only recognized Allah during emergencies, we would be treating an ever-present reality as though it were occasional and rare.
Narrator: [encouraging] So here's a simple practice for this week, before checking your phone tomorrow morning, spend thirty seconds noticing that your body simply worked again, unasked.
Narrator: It sounds small, almost too small to matter, but gratitude built on ordinary mornings tends to survive difficult ones far better than gratitude built only on extraordinary relief.
Narrator: [carefully] That's our reflection for today. However your morning began, I hope you notice it a little differently tomorrow.
